description_full: Everpure, Inc. provides data storage and management technologies, products, and services in the United States and internationally. Its Purity software is shared across its products and provides enterprise-class data services, such as always-on data reduction, data protection, and encryption, as well as storage protocols, such as block, file, and object. The company also provides FlashArray, including FlashArray//ST, FlashArray//X, FlashArray//C, FlashArray//XL, FlashArray//E, and FlashArray File Services, addressing databases, applications, virtual machines, and other traditional workloads; and FlashBlade integrated hardware systems comprising FlashBlade//S, FlashBlade//E, and FlashBlade//EXA for managing and processing unstructured data workloads of various types from real-time log analytics and commercial high-performance computing (HPC) to data protection and recovery. In addition, it offers cloud storage solutions, such as Portworx by Everpure, a cloud-native Kubernetes data management solution; and Evergreen/One; and Evergreen/Flex. Further, the company provides Everpure Fusion, a Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) management plane, which enables storage administrators to unify storage arrays and optimize storage pools; Evergreen Architecture comprising Pure1, an AI-driven cloud-based management platform, as well as Evergreen//One and Evergreen//Flex data storage solutions; and Everpure Cloud, a virtual block storage array, that provides customers the flexibility to operate a hybrid cloud model with seamless data mobility across on-premises and public cloud environments. It sells its products and subscription services through a direct sales force and channel partners. Everpure, Inc. has a strategic alliance with Odine Solutions Teknoloji Ticaret ve Sanayi A.S. The company was formerly known as Pure Storage, Inc. and changed its name to Everpure, Inc. in February 2026. Everpure, Inc. was incorporated in 2009 and is headquartered in Santa Clara, California.

financial_summary: Everpure, Inc. is a large-cap technology business with a $32.2B market cap on $3.7B of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at +10% over the past three years and +18% annually across the full decade, a respectable pace for a business of this size. Operating margins are expanding by +4.1pp year-over-year, which is one of the strongest signals that the moat is deepening.
Returns on capital run at 7% against a 11% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests. Gross margins of 69% confirm genuine pricing power.

The business throws off $616M in free cash flow — roughly 17 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 4.68× so those profits are backed by real cash.
Accruals are elevated at -14.8% of assets, and Sloan showed firms building earnings through accruals rather than cash systematically underperform.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and interest coverage of 34× is fortress-like.

Shareholder yield is only 1.1%, a thin return of capital, and stock-based comp at 13% of revenue is silent dilution an owner has to account for, and insiders hold 4.4% of the shares, and profit capture is only 0.1× the fair share, suggesting no structural edge inside its industry.

prof: ROIC of 7% falls short of the cost of capital of 11.4%, so growth at these returns destroys value.

Earnings quality is mixed: cash conversion of 4.68x, but high accruals (-14.8% of assets).
ROE of 13% is amplified by 3.2x balance-sheet leverage (DuPont), so ROIC is the cleaner read on the business.

hlth: The balance sheet carries net cash of $629.6M.

growth: Revenue has compounded at 10.0% over 3 years, 16.8% over 5 years and 17.5% over 10 years, so growth is decelerating, and it has been lumpy (year-to-year swings of 12%).
At current returns, reinvesting 100% of profits supports about 6.6% a year of fundamental growth, enough to sustain growth.
Free cash flow has compounded 46.0% a year over five years.
Forward indicators: a book-to-bill of 1.30 (orders outpacing sales), a backlog worth 1.0x annual revenue and deferred revenue up 24%.
Capex runs 1.9x depreciation (7.2% of sales), so it is building capacity for future growth.
own: Insiders own a modest 4.4%, and institutions hold 87%.

Shareholder yield is a modest 1.1% (1.1% in buybacks).
people: With about 6,400 employees, each generates about $572K of revenue, 1.5x the Technology median, and productivity has risen 17.5% a year.
That works out to $96K of free cash flow per employee.
The company is founder-led, which often keeps management aligned with long-term owners.
CEO pay is $2.4M (4x revenue per employee), and compensation governance scores poorly (9/10, lower is better).
